Filters

2 includes both +2% and −2% or larger.
Your other filters apply first. Then exactly this many tiles are shown, ranked by price × volume. Pick 50 and you get 50 tiles whenever at least 50 stocks pass the filters.
Comma-separated tickers create a custom selection within the chosen market.
The index dropdown selects one universe at a time. Companies with more than one listed share class (for example GOOG and GOOGL) are combined into a single tile. Filter choices save on this device and are restored next time. For theme, tile labels and layout, use Appearance.

Bring your own snapshot

Import a CSV or JSON file with these columns: symbol, name, price, percent_change, market_cap, volume, sector, industry. Use percentages as numbers: 2 means +2%, not 0.02. Dollar values can use B, M or T suffixes. Optional columns: is_sp500, is_nasdaq100, is_dow30, as_of. A bare number means dollars, not billions.

Membership for the S&P 500 comes from the daily snapshot. Companies with multiple listed share classes (for example Alphabet's GOOG and GOOGL, Berkshire Hathaway's A and B shares, or Fox's FOXA and FOX) are combined into one tile: volume and price × volume are added across classes, while market cap uses the largest class figure, because the source data reports close to the full company value on each class rather than a per-class slice. Nasdaq 100 and Dow 30 use constituent lists captured November 2, 2026; they can change. Russell 1000, Russell 2000 and Russell 3000 are approximated from the snapshot by market-cap rank (top 1,000; ranks 1,001 to 3,000; top 3,000) rather than official constituent lists. Logos are embedded for the original index stocks and requested from public logo hosts for additional symbols. A small outlined mark means a logo is unavailable, not a company logo.

Your settings and imported data stay in this browser. Opening the page or tapping Refresh pulls the latest delayed quotes from CNBC, about 15 minutes behind the exchange, for prices, daily change, volume and market cap, with TradingView as a backup feed if CNBC cannot be reached; new logos contact public image hosts. The map opens on the snapshot saved with this page, with its date shown in the header, and live quotes swap in automatically when a feed answers; when no feed can be reached the saved snapshot stays on screen and the page keeps retrying. The snapshot is also the source of sector, industry and index membership data. The quote feed offers no service guarantee, and the snapshot collection time is not a quote time.

Delayed quotes: CNBC, with TradingView as backup. Period performance (1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y): TradingView scanner performance fields. Daily snapshot (sector, industry and index membership; fallback quotes): Top US Stock Tickers / Nasdaq snapshot. Logos: NVSTly. Membership lists: Slickcharts. Individual company marks belong to their owners.
